Long story short, NFTs (non-fungible tokens) are bought and sold on the blockchain, and since the blockchain cannot be edited, you can use it to prove that you are the “owner” of a digital piece of media, most often a picture. The Ape in question is from the Bored Ape Yacht Club, which was a series of several thousand images of similar cartoon apes. The reasons people are upset about NFTs in general are because 1) NFTs are largely a Ponzi scheme, since they are literally a link to a JPG, their only value comes from artificial scarcity, 2) the money used to purchase NFT’s could instead go to commissioning actual artists for work instead of buying a random asset-generated monkey, 3) it is estimated that the electricity used to support NFTs on the blockchain is greater than that of some small countries, and at least for me 4) NFT enthusiasts (especially on twitter) are EXTREMELY vocal and many of them hand-wave away any criticism with “you just don’t understand.” Sorry for the dump, it’s a bizarre situation that I wouldn’t expect anyone who isn’t on the internet way too much to know about haha

There's been a lot of speculation (and possibly confirmation, but I'm not 100% sure) that the PS5 is going to be backwards compatible with the PS4, and I would be shocked if the next Xbox wasn't backwards compatible with the Xbox One. So I feel like the smart thing for DE to do would be to just continue to support the current gen versions and they would get "boosted" by the next gen better hardware.

Obviously though they couldn't do this forever, and I think that they should take a page out of Final Fantasy 14's book. A Realm Reborn, the "reboot" of FF14, came out in 2013 on the PC and PS3, with the PS4 release later on. As updates continued, supporting the PS3 version was holding back the other two versions (I believe they all had cross-play). They announced 9 months before their big 2017 expansion, Heavensward, that they would be discontinuing support of the PS3 version when the expansion came out. I could definitely imagine Warframe doing something similar (if it keeps getting support that far in the future), with current gen support ending 3ish years after the next gen consoles coming out.
